recent_posts.title: Platform strategy is about enabling evolution, not driving innovation
recent_posts.summary: Platform teams don't need to be innovation leaders to be strategic. Their role is to enable architectural evolution by adopting external innovations and making them accessible to application teams. Effective platform strategy involves watching industry trends and gradually introducing tools that support natural technology progression, from containerization to cloud migration to elastic scaling. This incremental approach provides application teams with flexibility to innovate while maintaining system stability across large organizations.

recent_posts.title: Things I Currently Believe About AI and Tech Employment
recent_posts.summary: As AI innovation continues to evolve, its impact on engineering roles and tech employment remains uncertain. There is ongoing debate about whether AI will eliminate the need for junior or mid-level engineers, with some startups hiring primarily junior talent for early-stage development. The future of engineering roles may involve specialization and changes in career paths rather than significant reduction in demand for engineers. While AI boosts productivity, it is unclear if this will significantly impact long-term demand for software-based products.

recent_posts.title: Some Tips for Moderating a Successful Panel
recent_posts.summary: Moderating a successful panel requires writing individual questions for each panelist and researching them to tailor discussions effectively. It's important to prepare questions ahead, focus on specific themes, and prevent overwhelming participants with questions. Moderators should actively manage discussions and limit their own speaking to ensure the panelists remain the focus.

recent_posts.title: 10 Years of Engineering Ladders
recent_posts.summary: The post reflects on the 10-year anniversary of publishing the Rent the Runway engineering career ladder. It highlights the impact of the publicly shared ladder on the tech industry, providing initial guidelines for creating meaningful ladders. The author also shares advice on building effective ladders and discusses the continuing relevance of hierarchical structures in organizations despite emerging trends for flat structures.

recent_posts.title: The Senior Shortcut
recent_posts.summary: The trend towards hiring only senior engineers due to AI displacing simple tasks is shortsighted. The distinction between 'senior' and 'junior' engineers is evolving, with 'early career' becoming a preferred term. Companies benefit from nurturing early career engineers, who eventually grow into valuable senior positions. Over-reliance on hiring externally for senior roles can backfire as these individuals may struggle to adapt to the company's culture. Investing in early career hires fosters long-term growth and adaptability within the organization.

recent_posts.title: Platform Engineering Beyond CFEngine
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the evolution and limitations of traditional configuration management systems like CFEngine in modern platform engineering. It highlights the challenges of maintaining heterogenous environments and the shortcomings of relying heavily on tools like Terraform. The post argues for the importance of platform teams not just in configuration management, but in building and operating abstractions that simplify application deployment and reduce operational burdens for teams. Instead of focusing on enabling scripts and automation, it advises creating products that address common deployment needs efficiently.

recent_posts.title: Following The Manager’s Path
recent_posts.summary: Platform Engineering: A Guide for Technical, Product, and People Leaders is a forthcoming book co-authored by Ian Nowland and aims to build on the management lessons of The Manager’s Path. The book delves into the evolution of software infrastructure and the challenges of platform engineering teams. It emphasizes the need for different management skills, agile practices, and balancing long-term initiatives with regular operational duties. The author shares insights on handling these complexities to help leaders improve engineering operations amidst the growing demands of modern software.

recent_posts.title: Founders Create Managers
recent_posts.summary: The post critiques the concept of 'founder mode' described in a popular article, arguing that it can lead to manipulation by senior executives when founders micromanage instead of trusting their team. It suggests that the key to preventing this is establishing effective systems of accountability and fostering a strong, ethical company culture that encourages transparency and trust.
